stories.title: Reggie Wayne jokes about needing to become a player-coach after Colts trade away Josh Downs, Keenan Allen
stories.summary: Wayne played for the Colts from 2001 to 2014 and is a member of the team's Ring of Honor.
stories.detail: The 2026 NFL trade deadline was Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. The Indianapolis Colts are 2-7 and in third place in the AFC South. Given how the season has gone so far, the Colts continued their restructuring by offloading wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday. Former Colts wide receiver Reggie Wayne, who has been Indy's WR coach since 2022, posted on social media after the deadline, joking that he may need to dust off his cleats and become a player-coach to help address the team's lack of depth. Welp... Might be time to dust off the old Reeboks.... 🤷🏾‍♂️ Has the player-Coach thing ever happened before? pic.twitter.com/i0CWCrPLAI — Reggie Wayne (@ReggieWayne_17) November 10, 2026 Wayne played for the Colts from 2001 to 2014. Over his career, he amassed 14,345 receiving yards and 82 touchdowns. To answer Wayne's question, yes, player-coaches have been a thing, but he is not eligible because the current Collective Bargaining Agreement bans that option. The last player-coach was Dan Reeves for the Dallas Cowboys in the early 1970s. Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs along with a 2027 seventh-round pick for a 2027 fourth- and fifth-round pick. Allen went to the San Fr…

stories.title: Is the NFC East really winnable by the Cowboys?
stories.summary: Do you still believe in the Cowboys?
stories.detail: Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys kept their hopes alive for the 2026 season this past Sunday. They managed to actually snatch a victory from the jaws of defeat instead of the other way around. The 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts wasn’t exactly high-quality football, but a win is a win when it comes to making the playoffs. And that is what we are here to discuss – do you believe the Cowboys can still make the playoffs? Obviously, technically, they can. They are a long way from being mathematically eliminated. But do you believe in them, or have you lost hope? At 4-5, they trail the 5-2-1 New York Giants who are currently going through QB issues due to injury. The Giants keep winning by beating bad teams, something the Cowboys have not been as good at. The Cowboys wasted some of their soft schedule while the Giants mostly made good on theirs. So do you believe the Cowboys can win the NFC East and make the playoffs? The second half of the season gets harder for the Cowboys, but the same can be said of the Giants. What’s your call BTB? stories.title: Giants' Nabers calls Fox analyst Olsen's body language critique a 'lie'
stories.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after the game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and being a bad teammate was a "lie."
stories.detail: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after Sunday's game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and the insinuation that he's a bad teammate was a "lie." Nabers was intent on speaking up for himself against some of the things said about him on the broadcast. "The thing about it is, don't tell the world something that's not me," Nabers said. "I'm speaking for myself all the time because there is nobody else that is going to be able to speak up for me. So I'm going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. "I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I've never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of." The Fox broadcast showed Nabers seemingly upset during the Giants' 19-11 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles . Nabers had five catches on eight targets for 43 yards in the win, the first time since Week 3 that he has been held to fewer than 100 yards. It was Nabers' first career victory in Philadelphia and …

teamStories.title: Vikings reunite with QB Kirk Cousins, send 3rd-round pick to Raiders
teamStories.summary: Vikings are trading for quarterback Kirk Cousins, sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders.
teamStories.detail: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Vikings reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders on Tuesday, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas. With the trade, 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' starting quarterback, beginning this week at home against the Seattle Seahawks . Aidan O'Connell will be Mendoza's backup. Cousins posted a goodbye to the Raiders on his Instagram story, writing, "Thank you Raiders Nation! Go get em @fernandomendoza." Trade talks between the teams didn't materialize until Tuesday, according to Las Vegas general manager John Spytek, who said the team was not actively looking to trade Cousins. Spytek said he received a few phone calls about Cousins until the most important one came from Vikings GM Nolan Teasley. He and Teasley spoke on the phone for a while to hammer down the framework on a deal that made sense for both sides. Spytek said he did not speak to Cousins before Tuesday about the possibility of him being traded. "There was nothing to speak about," Spytek said. "We didn't have any expectation that this was coming." Once a trade appeared to be a reality, Spytek and coach Klint Kubiak sat down with Cousins to presen…

teamStories.title: Raiders sign DL Tim Keenan to the active roster from the practice squad
teamStories.summary: The Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, leaving an open roster spot.
teamStories.detail: The Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, leaving an open roster spot. They filled it by signing rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-player roster from the practice squad. Keenan was out of elevations from the practice squad after the Raiders elevated him for the past three games. In three games, Keenan totaled seven tackles and a sack while playing 35 percent of the snaps. The Rams selected Keenan in the seventh round this year out of Alabama. They waived him out of the preseason, but he signed back to their practice squad. The Raiders signed him to their practice squad on Sept. 7. The team also announced it signed defensive tackle Chris Williams to the practice squad.

teamStories.summary: Which teams made the best -- and worst -- moves before the NFL trade deadline? We're making sense of all the action.
teamStories.detail: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. I will forever remember it as the trade deadline in which the Bengals nearly accidentally traded a third-round pick for Arnold Ebiketie (more on that below). Identifying winners and losers on deadline day is always tough. The Titans, Howie Roseman and Josh Downs will be made winners and losers for their efforts not by my words but by the picks they make or games they win over the next two or three years. Of course, we can grade the quality of their work now (spoiler, they are winners) -- but this isn't the real test. The real test is what comes next . I have six winners and four losers from this year's trade deadline ranging from players to GMs. Let's dive in. No, he won't set the passing touchdown record or anything. But let's trace the arc here. Cousins started nine games for a 4-5 Raiders team that was waiting to turn the page to 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza . teamStories.summary: Tim Keenan promoted from practice squad
teamStories.detail: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an unsurprising move, the Las Vegas Raiders signed rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Keenan takes the roster spot left vacant from the Raiders’ trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minensota Vikings for a third-round draft pick in 2027. It was likely Keenan would soon be added to the 53-man roster. He was elevated from the practice squad for the past three games, which is the elevation limit for a season. Keenan was a seventh-round draft pick of the Los Angeles Rams this year out of Alabama. He was waived in September. The Raiders then signed him to their practice squad. Keenan played in all three games he was elevated for and he even started in Week 9 at San Francisco, playing a season high 49 percent of the snaps. He has played in 35 percent of the snaps in his three games. He has a total of seven tackles with four coming against the 49ers. Expect him to continue to be part of the playing rotation for the rest of the season. To replace Keenan on the practice squad, the Raiders signed defensive tackle Chris Williams. He has been in the NFL since 2020 and was part of the Falcons’…

stories.title: NBA issues retroactive flagrant foul to Keldon Johnson after officials missed his blatant groin kick of Devin Booker
stories.summary: NBA officials need to do better.
stories.detail: Keldon Johnson got away with shenanigans in real time. But the NBA’s not letting him off the hook. The NBA announced Tuesday that it’s issued a postgame flagrant foul 1 to the San Antonio Spurs guard for an infraction during Monday’s blowout win over the Phoenix Suns. The infraction? He kicked Devin Booker in the groin, very clearly so. Booker went down to the court in obvious pain. But game officials chose to move along as if nothing happened. Here’s the incriminating video that the Suns were happy to post on their social media Tuesday. Tuesday, Keldon Johnson was assessed a postgame Flagrant Foul Penalty 1 for his kick on Devin Booker in Monday's game. The play was not reviewed in real-time. pic.twitter.com/z3lxCWdjIN — PHNX Suns (@PHNX_Suns) November 10, 2026 That isn’t subtle. Referee Natalie Sago was standing with a clear view of the infraction, and nothing was called on the floor. So play ensued as Booker writhed in pain on the court until the Suns were forced to call a timeout. But there was a chance to rectify the situation from there. Per the NBA rulebook , coaches aren’t permitted to challenge a non-call. Suns coach Jordan Ott had no recourse to initiate a replay review.…

stories.title: Warriors lose guard Brandon Williams to mild hamstring strain
stories.summary: The Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's win, sources told ESPN.
stories.detail: The Golden State Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's 138-87 win over the New Orleans Pelicans , the team announced Tuesday. Williams entered late in the first quarter, burst to the rim for two quick layups but came up hobbled on the second and limped to the locker room after only 99 seconds of action. The Warriors soon announced that Williams was out with a hamstring issue and scheduled for an MRI. Those results revealed the mild strain, ruling him out for the Warriors' difficult upcoming road trip to Houston, San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis. Williams has been an immediate bench spark in his first season with the Warriors, averaging 10.4 points and 2.3 assists in only 16.4 minutes per game, providing scoring punch the moment Stephen Curry rests. Williams has 17 and 20 points in the two games that Curry missed this season, including a win over the LA Clippers as part of the Warriors' current eight-game win streak. But left hamstring issues have followed Williams early in his NBA career. He strained it in the 2025 preseason while with Dallas and subsequently missed time la…
